![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186068697/plots/c381d7409e7b3f60ec5755809135c723ef9bd4155da21c438e1625b6b1246692.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following statements are true? 

I. $f(x)$ is **not** defined at $x=0$
II. ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=f(0)$
III. $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is false. Indeed, $f(x)$ is defined at $x=0$ and $f(0)=5.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, from the graph we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x) & =5, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x) & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=5=f(0).$

- Statement III is true. The graph of $f(x)$ can be drawn without taking our pencil off of the paper in the neighborhood of $x=0.$
